sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - Marketplace FBA Store

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, entered into force 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Proceeds of Crime and Terrorist Financing Reporting and Recordkeeping Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 83.01 et seq.; United Nations Act, S.C. 2000, c. 41; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 22; British Columbia Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 348, Pt. 3; British Columbia Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21.1-21.6 and Beneficial Ownership Regulations, SOR/2019-258

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified true copy of passport of each non-resident general partner and each beneficial owner meeting the 25% threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed notary public or competent legal authority in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent apostille authority of the origin country, or consular legalization at a Canadian embassy or consulate if the origin country is not a Hague Apostille Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction corporate registry or registered agent of the corporate general partner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the BC registered agent and the law firm for pre-incorporation filings and service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of signing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of Funds and Source of Wealth affidavit executed by each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed notary public or certified legal counsel

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and professional third-party reference letter (if bank facility is maintained for the LP)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution and licensed professional, respectively, with notarization of signatures

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons per FINTRAC guidance; real-time screening of all UBOs, general partners, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, and the Criminal Code terrorist entities list; ongoing transaction monitoring and annual re-screening for any changes in control or ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registry Online operated by the British Columbia Corporate Registry (www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A proposed limited partnership name must be expressed in English or French (or a bilingual combination), contain a distinctive element, an optional descriptive element, and a mandatory legal element such as 'Limited Partnership', 'LP', 'L.P.', or 'société en commandite'. Non-Latin script must be transliterated into an acceptable English or French phonetic form using the Latin alphabet; numerals and special characters are subject to registrar discretion.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the BC Registrar rejects a name reservation, the applicant will receive a rejection notice stating the grounds. The applicant may submit a written reconsideration request through BC Registry Online within 30 days, including a revised name, explanatory submissions, and any required consent letters. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may commence judicial review before the British Columbia Supreme Court under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, and the applicable provisions of the Business Corporations Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable. A BC limited partnership used as an Amazon FBA e-commerce seller may maintain its registered office at the office of a licensed BC registered agent or a reputable commercial virtual-office provider, provided that the address is a physical location in British Columbia at which process can be served during normal business hours and required statutory records can be inspected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (less than 5% probability over a three-year period for a low-risk online marketplace retail operation). CRA and BC Ministry of Finance audits are ordinarily documentary by mail; an unannounced physical inspection generally occurs only upon a clear audit trigger, such as unreported revenue flags, material GST/PST input credit mismatches, or third-party information, and FINTRAC on-site inspection does not apply to this non-regulated LP.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and name reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the BC Business Corporations Act fee schedule, approximately CAD 40.
Statutory filing fee for a declaration of limited partnership under the BC Partnership Act.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and BC resident agent service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of CAD 150 to CAD 250 for a BC registered office plus agent service.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO, PEP, and sanctions screening per individual beneficial owner and signatory
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance service provider or retained law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for automated screening plus professional review, approximately USD 60 to USD 120 per individual.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, and consular legalization bundle (five documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary, apostille authority, and Canadian consular office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 60 to USD 120 per document, plus expedited courier and foreign official fees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stage 1 legal due diligence and pre-incorporation opinion (name clearance, UBO analysis, partnership tax classification, and LP agreement preparation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Canadian business law firm in British Columbia
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of CAD 1,800 to CAD 3,000 for a fixed-fee Stage 1 engagement.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348, Part 5 (ss. 55–95) for limited partnership registration; Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 for governance of a corporate general partner, if used.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statement of Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LP-1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a British Columbia limited partnership. Capital contributions are established in the limited partnership agreement, and no escrow or deposit account is mandated at registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the General Partner of the Limited Partnership: (1) the Statement of Registration filed under the Partnership Act (British Columbia) is approved, and the General Partner is authorized to complete and submit the same; (2) the British Columbia registered office identified in the Statement of Registration is adopted as the continuing office for service of process; (3) the General Partner is authorized to execute the limited partnership agreement and to accept capital subscriptions from limited partners; (4) such officers, managers, or agents as the General Partner designates are appointed to open banking and payment accounts and to conduct Amazon FBA and e-commerce operations; and (5) these resolutions take effect upon issuance of the Certificate of Registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Online Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name availability search against British Columbia business registries, submit a Name Reservation Request, pay the applicable fee, and obtain a reservation valid for 56 days. Include three alternative names in order of preference and avoid restricted words without regulatory consent.
required_dossiers: Three alternate names in priority order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for being not distinctive or confusingly similar, resubmit a revised name reservation, apply the examiner's comments, or file an appeal with the District Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Organic Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and legal advisors; notarization or witness signing as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Limited Partnership Agreement and the Statement of Registration for a Limited Partnership (Form LP-1). Obtain execution by all general partners, attach a subscription schedule identifying limited partners and agreed capital contributions, and obtain the consent of each proposed registered office. Non-resident limited partners may be included if disclosed in the statement.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement signed by all general partners
Limited partners' subscription and capital contribution schedule
Consent to act of each general partner
Consent to use of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any document is incomplete, amend and re-execute it before filing. Post-filing corrections are cured by filing an amendment to the Statement of Registration with the registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies via BC Registries and Online Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Statement of Registration and required attachments electronically through BC Corporate Online. Pay the registration filing fee at submission. Upon approval, the registrar issues the Certificate of Registration and assigns the BC partnership registration number.
required_dossiers: Identification details of all general partners
Legal counsel representation letter, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a deficiency notice, correct the stated particulars and resubmit within the notice period without a new filing fee where permitted. If registration lapses, pay the reactivation fee and refile within the applicable cure window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Business Number Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Certificate of Registration issuance, create the partnership record with the Canada Revenue Agency to obtain a federal Business Number. Register for GST/HST when gross revenue exceeds CAD 30,000 or voluntarily; register for BC PST if there is selling presence or a collection obligation; register as an employer with CRA and WorkSafeBC if employees are engaged.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Statement of Registration
Identification of general partners and limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA online application is rejected, verify legal-name matching with the Certificate of Registration, contact the CRA business line with proof of registration, or submit the paper RC business registration form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office, Municipal and Occupational Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry; local municipal licensing authority; WorkSafeBC; local fire authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain statutory records at the registered office, including the limited partnership agreement and limited partner register. Verify whether the municipality where the registered office or fulfillment warehouse is located requires a general business licence or property-use permit. For any physical inventory location, complete the applicable fire safety inspection and occupational health registration.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application, if applicable
Fire safety inspection report, if a warehouse is used
WorkSafeBC registration confirmation, if workers are present
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal licensing is refused, correct the zoning defect by seeking a temporary use permit or relocating the registered office or warehouse to a permitted commercial zone. Fire clearance deficiencies are cured by installing required suppression systems, emergency egress, and alarm equipment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Continuing Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and BC registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble the minute book or statutory record book, file the original Certificate of Registration, retain the executed Limited Partnership Agreement, record the general partner's service details, and calendar the annual statutory report. Limited partners have no management authority, and the general partner exercises exclusive management control.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If annual report filing is later missed, remedy by filing the late annual report and paying the prescribed late fee before the registrar initiates dissolution or strike-off proceedings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board is applicable to pure e-commerce marketplace resale in British Columbia. Occupational safety oversight is vested in WorkSafeBC and local fire authorities where premises are occupied.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No manufacturing or physical retail operating permit is required for ISIC 4791 retail sale via internet and Amazon FBA general operations. A municipal business licence may be required by the local government where the partnership maintains a physical office, warehouse, or inventory.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Environmental Assessment Office and BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for pure online marketplace resale; no environmental assessment certificate is required unless warehousing or ancillary activities create prescribed emissions, effluent, or hazardous waste triggers under the Environmental Management Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emission obligations apply to third-party fulfillment operations. If the partnership directly operates a warehouse, comply with municipal sewer and stormwater bylaws, British Columbia Recycling Regulation for packaging and electronic products, and federal hazardous waste and WHMIS rules for returned goods.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If commercial premises are leased, obtain an occupancy permit or fire safety inspection under the BC Fire Code and maintain fire suppression, emergency egress, and panic hardware. Register with WorkSafeBC before engaging workers. Virtual and third-party-logistics FBA operations require no additional physical clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — federal income tax, GST/HST and payroll administration; national portals: My Business Account (MyBA), Business Registration Online (BRO), and GST/HST NETFILE for mandatory electronic filing; Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) — export reporting via the Canadian Export Reporting System (ERS) and the CARM single-window platform; British Columbia Ministry of Finance — BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) and Employer Health Tax administered through eTaxBC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Limited Partnership extraprovincially with the BC Registry (Corporate Online) to establish legal existence in the jurisdiction. Step 2: Apply to CRA for a 15-character Business Number (BN) with program accounts using Form RC1 or BRO; the LP itself (not the individual partners) must open an RT (GST/HST) program account because the Excise Tax Act treats a partnership as a distinct person for GST/HST, even though the LP is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes. Step 3: Open an RP payroll account if BC employees are engaged, and register for BC Employer Health Tax (triggered where annual BC remuneration exceeds CAD 500,000) and WorkSafeBC coverage. Step 4: Open an RM import/export account with CBSA if the LP will self-clear cross-border shipments. Non-resident partners do not obtain Canadian TINs; they report their allocated Canadian-source income under their home-country TINs and file, where required, T5013/T1/T2 returns with CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — Canadian Limited Partnership is a full flow-through conduit under ITA s. 96; no entity-level income tax; each partner is taxable on its agreed share of Canadian-source income. Territorial scope: non-resident partners are taxed in Canada only on Canadian-source income allocated by the LP, subject to applicable tax treaty protection. The LP remains a separate registrable person for GST/HST under ETA s. 2(1). FBA inventory stored in Canadian fulfilment centres may create a fixed-place-of-business permanent establishment risk for non-resident partners under certain tax treaties (OECD 2017 commentary); PE mitigation requires analysis of the Amazon FBA Seller Agreement and the partner's broader Canadian activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; entity classification is statutory. Available elections: (i) ITA s. 96(3) joint partnership/partner election for alternative income or loss allocation; (ii) ITA s. 249.1(4) non-calendar fiscal-period election; (iii) ETA s. 273 election between a registrant and a closely related corporation or partner to treat intercompany taxable supplies as made for nil consideration, eliminating GST/HST on internal recharges; (iv) ETA s. 211.2 fulfilment-seller exception under which a non-resident seller that is itself a GST/HST registrant may displace the online platform's deemed-supplier status, subject to the platform operator's due diligence; (v) simplified non-resident GST/HST registration regime for remote e-commerce suppliers with no Canadian residency or permanent establishment requirement.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal value-added tax: Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5%; British Columbia is a non-HST province, so the 7% BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) is imposed separately at retail, producing a combined 12% consumer tax burden in BC. Under the July 1, 2021 e-commerce platform rules, Amazon as marketplace operator is generally deemed to make the supply and must collect and remit GST/HST and BC PST on sales of FBA goods located in Canada at the time of sale.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST small-supplier threshold: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies in Canada in a single calendar quarter or across the four preceding calendar quarters. Non-resident remote sellers operating through their own channels must register once the CAD 30,000 threshold is exceeded; goods stored in Canadian fulfilment centres and sold through a deemed-supplier platform are taxed at the platform level with no registration threshold for the underlying seller. BC PST: out-of-province sellers engaged in business in BC must register with the BC Ministry of Finance, with a de minimis remote-seller relief where BC taxable sales are CAD 10,000 or less in the preceding 12 months.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or API-based e-invoicing mandate currently exists in Canada or BC. Registrants must issue a proper GST/HST tax invoice containing prescribed particulars within 15 days after the end of the month of the supply; electronic records are accepted under ETA s. 286 provided they are legible, complete and retained in a CRA-approved format. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically via NETFILE once annual gross revenue exceeds CAD 1,000,000. Canada is voluntarily adopting the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Service (PEPPOL network), but there is no legislative clearance API. Amazon Seller Central and the Amazon Marketplace Tax Report function as the transactional e-invoice and sales-data backbone for audit substantiation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under ETA Sch. VI Part V s. 1 to the supply of goods exported by the supplier with proof of export, and under Part V s. 7 to services supplied to non-residents and performed for use exclusively outside Canada. For Amazon FBA, sales delivered to Canadian addresses attract 5% GST (plus 7% BC PST or the applicable provincial HST); sales of goods actually exported from Canada to foreign delivery addresses can be zero-rated only where the LP (or Amazon acting on its behalf) holds contemporaneous documentary proof of export. Transfers of the LP's inventory into Amazon's Canadian fulfilment centres are non-supply inventory movements and are not zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration (B13A/CAED) filed with CBSA through the Export Reporting System where shipment value exceeds CAD 2,000 or the goods are controlled or regulated
Commercial invoice (Amazon Seller Central output) showing FOB origin, HS tariff codes, unit values in CAD and purchaser details
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) in the shipper's name, or courier delivery manifest for DHL/FedEx/UPS parcel movements
Customs broker export and import release records (PARS/ERS acknowledgements) for goods transiting Canadian ports and border crossings
Foreign exchange receipt evidence: SWIFT MT103 credit advices, Airwallex/Stripe settlement statements, or bank inward remittance certificates evidencing repatriation of export proceeds in CAD
Marketplace order-log extracts demonstrating the non-resident status and foreign delivery address of each end consumer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits export zero-rating claims using Amazon marketplace order data, customs transit records and banking remittance documentation; missing export proof triggers reassessment of uncollected 5% GST/HST and BC PST, plus daily compound interest at the prescribed rate and a 5% default penalty escalating by 1% per month (maximum 12 months). False statements and gross negligence attract penalties up to 50% of the tax avoided, with criminal prosecution available under ITA s. 239 and ETA s. 328 carrying fines up to 200% of the tax and imprisonment. The normal four-year reassessment window extends to seven years by waiver and up to ten years for misrepresentation or fraud. All export substantiation records must be retained for at least six years from the date of the supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in coordination with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible with no exchange controls. Canada has accepted Article VIII obligations under the IMF Articles of Agreement since 1951, guaranteeing unrestricted current account and capital account convertibility. The Currency Act and Bank of Canada Act impose no conversion limitations. Profit remittance (dividends, partnership distributions) is free of foreign exchange restriction; however, non-resident distributions may attract Part XIII withholding tax (15% under Canada-US tax treaty reduced rate; otherwise 25%) and require Form NR4 filing by the partnership.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export proceeds surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio exists in Canada. Under the repealed Foreign Exchange Control Act (1951), all surrender requirements were eliminated. Exporters may freely hold foreign currency in Canadian-dollar or foreign-currency accounts. Cross-border electronic transfers of CAD 10,000 or more trigger FINTRAC reporting obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility with legal constraints. Canada has no EU-style EMI licensing regime. Airwallex, Wise, and Payoneer operate as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA, not as banks. They may hold funds but cannot create deposit liabilities or issue credit cards domestically without OSFI licensing under the Bank Act. Suitable for operational disbursement rails but not for primary capital escrow. MSB registration fee CAD 100 (annual renewal) and requires a compliance program with a designated Chief Compliance Officer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is generally mandatory for at least one general partner or authorized signatory at branch opening for Tier 1 banks, although several banks have introduced video KYC for personal accounts; corporate account opening consistently requires physical appearance or notarized/certified true copies of identification and corporate documents for non-resident signatories. Directors and all general partners must provide government-issued photo ID, proof of residential address, and the LP's certificate of registration. Remote opening for LPs with non-resident partners is typically rejected or escalated to enhanced due diligence review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership concentration (foreign limited partners holding >25% interest without Canadian nexus)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: LP agreement, registered declaration of partnership under BC Partnership Act, ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) table, passport copies of all partners, source of wealth/source of funds statements, and a Canadian nexus letter demonstrating commercial substance

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between declared business scope (Amazon FBA retail) and transaction profile (large cross-border wires, intercompany flows)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amazon seller central account verification, FBA inventory reports, commercial invoices, logistics contracts, marketplace payment reconciliation statements, and projected cash-flow model aligning transaction volumes

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: History < 12 months with no prior banking relationship (thin-file underwriting)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC registrar certificate of limited partnership, GST/HST registration confirmation (Canada Revenue Agency), EIN/BN documentation, audited or reviewed financial statements (if available), and detailed 24-month business plan with break-even analysis

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use of account for personal expenses by general partner (commingling of partnership and personal funds)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dedicated partnership bank statements, accounting separation policy, written operating resolution restricting personal withdrawals, and annual accountant attestation of commingling avoidance

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: OFAC/UN sanctions list screening hits on partner names or jurisdictions of fund origin
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global sanctions screening results from a commercial reputational database (e.g., Refinitiv/World-Check), partner declarations of non-sanctioned status, and jurisdictional source-of-funds trail from a FATF-compliant jurisdiction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of a Limited Partnership (BC Form LP-AR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Province of British Columbia (BC Registry Services)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months (60 days) after each anniversary of the limited partnership's registration date under the Partnership Act (British Columbia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 100 (approximately USD 73) if the annual report is submitted after the 60-day anniversary window; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to cancel the limited partnership's certificate, triggering administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (T5013 Slips, Summary, and Partner Allocations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the calendar year following the fiscal period end for a non-tax-shelter partnership; filing obligation is triggered whenever the limited partnership carries on business in Canada.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 40 per day per partner (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); for partnerships with annual gross revenue exceeding CAD 50,000, the penalty escalates to a CAD 500 base plus CAD 50 per day per partner to a maximum of CAD 7,500; each late or incorrect T5013 slip is subject to CAD 40 per slip, with further gross-negligence penalties under the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the Corporate General Partner (where the general partner is a CBCA federal corporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the general partner corporation's registration under the Canada Business Corporations Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No express monetary penalty is assessed for late filing; however, the corporate general partner remains in default and may be administratively dissolved by Corporations Canada after sustained non-filing, which would jeopardize continuity of the limited partnership's management and statutory validity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The Partnership Act (British Columbia) does not impose a mandatory independent audit on a non-reporting limited partnership. A statutory audit is triggered only where the limited partnership or its corporate general partner is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities legislation (National Instrument 81-106), where the Canada Revenue Agency specifically requests audited financial statements in support of the T5013 return, or where a lending or investment agreement contractually requires audited statements. For a typical privately held Amazon FBA e-commerce limited partnership, no compulsory external audit arises as a matter of corporate law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) as set out in CPA Canada Handbook Part II; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) under Part I is required only if the entity is a reporting issuer or voluntarily elects IFRS. Annual financial statements must be prepared in Canadian dollars, reconcile partner capital account balances, and support the T5013 income allocation schedule.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The BC Partnership Act does not require an annual beneficial-ownership confirmation filing for the limited partnership itself; however, the limited partnership must maintain an accurate Register of Limited Partners and record every transfer, assignment, or withdrawal of a partnership interest in the LP Register. Where the corporate general partner is incorporated under the CBCA, that corporation must maintain a register of significant individuals (holders of 25% or more of voting or controlling interests) and file any changes with Corporations Canada within 15 days of the change. It is recommended that beneficial-ownership details be re-confirmed from each partner annually at the time the BC Annual Report is prepared, and that partner identification documentation be retained in the general partner's corporate records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (names, addresses, contribution amounts, allocation ratios, and dates of admission or withdrawal)
Register of General Partners (names, management authority, and consent dates)
Records of Capital Contributions and Withdrawals (supported by executed partnership agreement amendments, bank statements, and distribution schedules)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180–350 per year for British Columbia registered-office and registered-agent services, including receipt and forwarding of statutory correspondence.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (no statutory audit is required); USD 2,000–6,000 for a review-engagement or notice-to-reader annual financial statement package; USD 8,000–15,000 for a full independent audit if demanded by a lender, investor, or the CRA.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% federal combined general corporate income tax rate, plus British Columbia provincial rate of 12% for a combined top statutory rate of 39% (2024). For active business income eligible for the federal small business deduction, the combined federal-provincial rate is approximately 11% (federal 9% plus BC 2%) up to the BC small business limit of C$500,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Limited Partnership is generally fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax purposes; no entity-level federal or BC income tax. Income is allocated to partners, who are taxed at their applicable rates. Non-resident partners are subject to Canadian non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII on deemed distributions of Canadian-source income allocated to them, unless reduced by treaty. No statutory tax holiday available to the described Amazon FBA retail business. Deductions include reasonable business expenses, CCA on eligible property, and arm's-length fees, subject to Canadian sourcing and documentation rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CRA Form T5013 Summary and T5013 Schedule (Information Return for a Partnership), filed electronically through CRA's Internet File Transfer / Represent a Client portal; partners receive T5013 slips. The LP is not required to file a corporation income tax return (T2) unless it elects to be treated as a corporation for certain purposes, which is atypical.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The partnership information return (T5013) must be filed no later than the day that is five months after the partnership's fiscal year-end. A nil or late return may extend assessment; installment obligations may apply to partners directly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 (Partnership Business Name and Business Number)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the LP and its CRA business number (BN) / partnership account number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the LP's Canadian BN. Non-resident partners must ensure the CRA has accurate foreign addresses and withholding obligations are correctly reflected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The reporting period end date, normally December 31 for calendar-year partnerships.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should align personal filings with the LP's fiscal year-end reported on T5013.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of partnership income/loss to each partner, including name, address, and share percentage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must report their Canadian-source allocated income in Part XIII withholding tax filings; treaty relief may reduce the rate but requires treaty eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 (Gross Revenue from Amazon FBA Sales)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross sales from e-commerce retail activities, including Amazon marketplace sales and associated shipping and handling revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Determine if a permanent establishment (PE) exists in Canada through the LP's activities or Amazon's deemed agency; if no PE, non-resident partners may be exempt from Canadian Part I tax on business income under the Canada-US treaty, but Part XIII withholding may still apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 20 (Cost of Goods Sold and Operating Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses including inventory costs, Amazon fees, fulfillment charges, advertising, software subscriptions, and administrative costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses reasonably incurred for earning Canadian-source income are deductible. Expenses recharged to a foreign related entity must satisfy arm's length and documentation standards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership net income or loss for the fiscal period before partner allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the LP has no PE in Canada, Canadian-source business income may be treaty-exempt for residents of treaty countries; nevertheless, T5013 filing may still be required if the partnership carries on business in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details of each partner's share, residency status, and allocated income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide each partner's country of residence, treaty country status, and valid Tax Identification Number. The partnership must withhold 15% non-resident tax on allocated Canadian-source income unless a reduced treaty rate applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty for T5013 returns is C$100 per partner per month, minimum C$1,000 and maximum C$8,000 per partnership (or C$2,500 and C$20,000 for specified partnerships). Gross negligence penalties up to 50% of understated tax may apply. Daily interest accrues on unpaid amounts at CRA prescribed rates.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Not directly applicable at the LP level because Canadian limited partnerships are tax transparent; distributions are generally treated as return of capital or income allocations. Part XIII withholding tax of 25% applies to amounts paid or credited to non-resident partners as income from Canadian-source partnership business or services, unless treaty reduced. For a Canadian corporation receiving dividends from a taxable Canadian corporation, the statutory rate is 25%, but that is outside the LP structure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident partner claiming reduced withholding under a tax treaty (e.g., Canada-US treaty, typically 15% on general business income absent a Canadian PE, or 5% for certain royalty income) must provide the partnership with a valid NR4 or NR301, or Form NR302 for treaty-based waiver. The recipient must be the beneficial owner and resident of a treaty country. Refund of excess withholding is available via filing a Canadian non-resident tax return (T1 or T3) within the normal statutory time limits, supported by a Certificate of Residence (e.g., US IRS Form 6166) from the treaty partner's tax authority.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Canadian withholding tax on interest paid to non-resident arm's-length lenders is generally exempt under domestic law (except participating interest), while non-arm's-length interest is subject to 25%, reduced to 15% under the Canada-US treaty, and in certain cases exempt under the Canada-US treaty interest article. Royalties paid to non-residents are subject to 25% statutory withholding; the Canada-US treaty generally reduces to 10% for copyright royalties and 0% for some literary, dramatic, musical, or artistic works; patent and know-how royalties generally 15% or 10% depending on the treaty and IP classification. The LP must obtain valid treaty documentation before applying reduced rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canadian transfer pricing documentation is required when the aggregate amount of transactions with non-resident non-arm's-length persons exceeds C$1 million for the taxation year. Since the LP is a partnership, the threshold applies at the partnership level. Contemporaneous documentation must be prepared by the partnership's filing due date. No separate Country-by-Country reporting obligation exists at the LP level unless consolidated group revenue exceeds C$750 million; such obligation rests with an ultimate parent that is a Canadian reporting entity.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split

Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) is most common for Amazon FBA distribution and retail service fees; CUP may be used for intercompany storage and fulfillment fees; profit split may be required if both parties contribute unique intangibles.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR), statutory anti-avoidance rules for partnerships, and the economic substance / business purpose doctrine under Canadian common law can deny tax benefits from transactions lacking genuine commercial substance. The LP must demonstrate real business activity, decision-making in Canada or through treaty-compliant management, and arm's length substance to avoid recharacterization by the CRA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Amazon FBA gross sales, concealing partner allocations, claiming fictitious expenses, or failing to file T5013 after carrying on business in Canada.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Canadian Income Tax Act, tax evasion is an indictable offense subject to fines of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years. Civil penalties include gross negligence penalties of 50% of understated tax plus interest and reinstated assessments without limitation periods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners of the LP may be jointly and severally liable for unremitted source deductions and withholding taxes; directors of a corporate general partner can face personal liability for unpaid corporate taxes under section 227.1 of the Income Tax Act. Criminal culpability can result in personal fines, restitution orders, travel bans, and imprisonment of up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or operating the LP without real business purpose, lacking Canadian management and control, using the partnership as a conduit to avoid Canadian tax, or structuring Amazon FBA sales to artificially avoid a PE status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may apply GAAR to deny tax benefits, recharacterize revenues, and impose reassessments with interest and penalties. A sham transaction can result in full reassessment of income to the beneficial owner and negligence penalties. The LP may also be struck for non-compliance under BC Partnership Act if it fails to maintain a registered office and filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners are personally liable for all LP debts and obligations if the LP is found to be a sham or lacking substance. Directors of corporate general partners may be liable for taxes, penalties, and interest; courts may impose personal civil restitution and travel bans pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Amazon FBA proceeds to launder funds, accepting proceeds of crime through payment rails, or misrepresenting beneficial ownership in anti-money laundering filings under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-compliance with AML registration (if the partnership is a money services business or engaged in MSB activities) can result in administrative monetary penalties up to C$1 million per violation for corporations, and criminal fines or imprisonment for individuals. CRA and FINTRAC enforcement can freeze accounts and assess penalties on unreported taxable benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior officers and directors who knowingly participate in or fail to prevent AML breaches face imprisonment up to five years and/or fines. Beneficial owners of the LP are subject to transparency reporting; concealment of true ownership is a criminal offense and may lead to personal liability, freezing orders, and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold Part XIII tax on income allocated to non-resident partners, failing to file NR4 or T5013 slips, or improperly claiming treaty benefits without establishing beneficial ownership and treaty residence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A 10% penalty on the amount of withholding tax required but not remitted (up to C$100 per slip per day for failure to file information returns); penalties may reach 25% of the unremitted amount for repeat failures. Interest accrues daily on unpaid liabilities. Directors of the general partner are personally liable for unremitted withholding taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are jointly and severally liable for the full amount of unremitted Part XIII tax, plus interest and penalties. Personal liability can be enforced through civil proceedings, asset garnishment, and travel bans if criminal tax evasion charges are laid.
